Procedure: Attended, full-night diagnostic polysomnography.

Surgical Pre-Operative Assessment
Pre-operative assessment of the patient is an important part of the surgical process. It is performed by a surgeon or a surgical assistant and involves a thorough examination of the patient's medical history, physical condition, and any other relevant information.
The purpose of the pre-operative assessment is to identify any potential risks or complications that may arise during the surgery and to ensure that the patient is fit for the procedure. This includes assessing the patient's general health, any existing medical conditions, and any medications they are taking.
During the pre-operative assessment, the patient will be asked about their medical history, including any previous surgeries, injuries, or illnesses. They will also be asked about any medications they are taking, as well as any allergies or sensitivities they may have.

In addition to the physical examination, the pre-operative assessment will also involve a discussion with the patient about the surgery itself. This will include a discussion of the risks and benefits of the procedure, as well as any alternatives that may be available.
